strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation: operating in intrinsic space rather than pixel space is principled and enables better preservation of geometry/materials while modifying weather effects

Intrinsic Map-Aware Attention (IMAA) mechanism: thoughtfully designed to address scale variation challenges in outdoor scenes; effective visualization demonstrates spatial correspondence benefits
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: comparisons across multiple method categories, multiple metrics, user study (61 participants, 81.67% preference), and ablation studies
Valuable dataset contributions: WeatherSynthetic (38k) and WeatherReal (18k) with intrinsic map annotations fill a gap in autonomous driving datasets with diverse weather coverage
Clear qualitative superiority: Figures 6-7 convincingly demonstrate preservation of scene geometry and materials compared to baselines that introduce artifacts or hallucinate objects
weaknesses: Temporal consistency limitation: framework does not guarantee frame-to-frame coherence in videos (Fig. 12), significantly limiting applicability for autonomous driving; limitation is acknowledged but dismissed as orthogonal rather than addressed substantively

WeatherReal dataset quality concerns: (1) circular dependency—uses inverse renderer to generate pseudo-labels then trains on WeatherReal, (2) manual validation rigor unclear—no disclosure of validation scale/criteria, (3) weather synthesis via Flux-Kontext may introduce systematic biases, (4) explicitly not used for evaluation raises generalization questions

Limited quantitative real-world evaluation: Table 3 inverse rendering uses own WeatherSynthetic test set; ACDC evaluation is indirect (via downstream tasks); TransWeather evaluation incomplete; most rigorous quantitative results on synthetic data only

Intrinsic decomposition validity assumptions: assumes perfect separation into weather-invariant materials/geometry and weather-variant illumination, but real effects involve complex interactions (rain reflections, fog depth perception, snow accumulation); single irradiance map may oversimplify complex real-world illumination

Extensive experimental validation including quantitative metrics across multiple aspects, comparisons with diverse baselines, ablation studies, and user study with perceptual evaluation
Valuable dataset contribution (WeatherSynthetic 35K + WeatherReal 18K) with intrinsic map annotations fills gap for outdoor driving scene resources
Strong quantitative results demonstrating superiority in plausibility (CLIP-S), structure preservation (DINO-ST), and downstream task performance on ACDC benchmark
Convincing visual quality in comparisons showing superior control and geometric/material preservation with minimal distortion or hallucination compared to pixel-space methods

Severe domain limitation: all experiments on outdoor driving scenes only; generalization to indoor/other domains unclear; design specifically tailored to this narrow use case
Computational efficiency completely unaddressed: no inference time comparisons, training cost analysis, or scalability discussion despite practical deployment importance

strengths: Well-motivated approach of performing weather editing in intrinsic space to preserve geometry and material properties, which is theoretically sound
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple datasets, metrics, baselines, ablation studies, and a user study
Contribution of two datasets (WeatherSynthetic: 35K, WeatherReal: 18K) with intrinsic map annotations that could benefit future research
Extensive supplementary material with additional experiments, ablations, and qualitative results demonstrating thorough documentation
Reasonable visual results showing the method can perform weather editing across diverse driving scenarios and indoor environments
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: IMAA is a simple gating mechanism (Eq. 4); both renderers are largely frozen pre-trained models with minimal fine-tuning; core contribution is primarily an engineering combination of existing techniques

Critical validation gap: No quantitative evaluation of intrinsic decomposition quality (albedo, normal, roughness, metallicity accuracy); paper relies on visual inspection and assumes heuristic-generated pseudo-labels are correct; no ground truth comparisons for intrinsic maps

Weak supervision throughout: Intrinsic maps generated via heuristics (gradient operators, DINO embeddings) rather than direct ground truth; no validation that pseudo-labels are accurate or that decomposition quality correlates with editing quality

Overstated controllability claims: Weather editing is limited to text prompts ('rainy', 'snowy') without fine-grained parameter control; claiming 'controllable' and 'fine-grained' weather synthesis is misleading

Missing critical baseline comparisons: No quantitative comparison with IntrinsicEdit (cited but not compared), IntrinsicRD, or recent intrinsic decomposition methods; comparison set limited to pixel-space methods and WeatherWeaver

Dataset quality concerns: WeatherSynthetic is purely synthetic (domain gap to real images); WeatherReal only 18K images; no validation of intrinsic map annotation quality; intrinsic maps are pseudo-labeled, not manually verified

Evaluation methodology issues: Quantitative metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) measure visual quality not decomposition accuracy; Table 3 has many missing entries; user study limited to 61 participants without statistical significance testing

Clear failure modes: Figure 25 shows hallucinations with dense fog; Figure 23 shows failures on out-of-distribution content (humans with snowflakes); temporal consistency not addressed despite autonomous driving motivation

Forward renderer limitations: Figure 10 shows WeatherWeaver sometimes produces more natural results; method struggles with extreme weather; some synthesized images appear unrealistic with unnatural lighting
Modest empirical gains from proposed components: IMAA improves PSNR by only 0.23 dB (23.58→23.81); unclear if this validates the proposed mechanism's effectiveness

Domain shift concerns: Method shows poor generalization to scenes and objects not in training data; acknowledged in Section 4.5 that temporal consistency (critical for video/autonomous driving) remains unaddressed

Reproducibility limitations: Code availability not mentioned; reliance on multiple frozen pre-trained models and dependencies; dataset release plans not discussed; training details scattered across supplementary
